runs.t: •  Ask: How many bedrooms are there?

slides.notes:
Welcome. Say: "Today: homes." Point to the house: "This is a house."
Before class: print the Student Pages (number expected + 3 spares), one set of picture cards per group of 3–4, the floor-plan picture for Talk Time, and the apartment ad for Real-World Reading. Have the phone + small speaker and L1_L10_listening.mp3 ready. Prep time: 30 min.
The apartment and the ad are invented. Never ask for real rent or real addresses. A dream home is fine.
Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. Say less, show more.
Class plan: 6:00 Hello + Review, 6:10 New Words, 6:20 Listening, 6:32 Grammar, 6:45 Break, 7:00 Talk Time, 7:10 Exit Ticket + Homework, 7:15 Real-World Reading, 7:25 Progress Check.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson10/Level1_Lesson10.md (At a glance, Clock-time plan, Teacher notes).

slides.title: Home Sweet Home

runs.t: I can name rooms and furniture.
I can say: There is… / There are…
I can ask: Is there a…? Are there…?
I can ask: How many… are there?
I can read an apartment ad.

slides.notes:
Click to show each goal, one at a time. Read it aloud. Learners repeat.
Goal 1: rooms and furniture: house, apartment, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, living room, bed, table, chair, sofa, refrigerator, window.
Goal 2: "There is a kitchen. There are two bedrooms."
Goal 3: "Is there a sofa?" "Are there windows?"
Goal 4: "How many bedrooms are there?" "There are two."
Goal 5: understand a simple apartment phone call; read an apartment ad (BR / BA / mo) at 7:15.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson10/Level1_Lesson10.md (At a glance: Objectives).
slides.title: Today's Goals

slides.notes:
Pairs. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. Late arrivals join any pair.
Before class, write on the board: When is your birthday? How's the weather today? Is there a kitchen?
Model with one learner: "When is your birthday?" "It's in May." Then "Is there a kitchen in your home?"
Click to show the A question. Click again for the B answers. Pairs use the Hello + Review page: 1 When is your birthday? 2 How's the weather today? 3 What day is today? It's ___. Switch. Then find a new partner.
Homework check (last 3 min): partners show last week's homework. Walk around and look.
New learners: pair them with a strong partner. If behind: one partner only.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson10/Level1_Lesson10.md (Step 1: Hello + Review; Student Pages: Hello + Review).

slides.title: Hello + Review

slides.notes:
Point to the floor plan: "Kitchen. Bedroom. Bathroom. Living room."
Click to show each picture. Point and say the word. Learners repeat 2 times. ★ words 2 more times.
Tip: apartment = a home in a building. house = a home that stands alone.
★ = most important words. If behind: teach the ★ words only.

slides.title: New Words

slides.notes:
Hold up the furniture cards: "Bed. Table. Chair. Sofa." Click to show each picture. Learners repeat 2 times.
Pairs (4 min): A points to a picture, B says the word. Then A asks "Is there a ___?" B answers "Yes, there is." / "No, there isn't."
★ = most important words. sofa, refrigerator, and window have no ★. If behind: teach the ★ words only.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson10/Level1_Lesson10.md (Step 2: New Words; Student Pages: New Words).

slides.notes:
Before you listen (1 min). Say: "Rosa calls about an apartment. She asks: Is there…? Are there…?"
Click to show each listen. Listen 1: Task A (check what the apartment has). Listen 2: Task B (circle the number of bedrooms and bathrooms). Listen 3: Task C (when is the rent due?).
Say it!: read each line. Learners repeat: "There are two bedrooms." "Is there a washing machine?"
The audio L1_L10_listening.mp3 (about 1:10) plays the conversation once. Press play again for the next listen. Pairs compare after each task. Write answers on the board.
No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer. The apartment is invented. Never ask learners for real rent.
Voices: Narrator, Agent, Rosa. Synthetic voices made with Chatterbox TTS (MIT), copied from short reference clips made with Kokoro-82M (Apache 2.0); no recordings of real people. Green Street Apartments is invented.
If behind: play 2 times; do Task C together.

slides.title: Before You Listen

slides.notes:
Listen 1 (Task A). Rosa calls about an apartment. Learners check ✓ what the apartment has.
Pairs compare. Then click to show each answer: two bedrooms ✓; washing machine ✗ ("No, there isn't."); refrigerator ✓; windows in the kitchen ✓; big living room ✓.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson10/Level1_Lesson10.md (Step 3: Listening; Student Pages: Listening A; Answer key, Listening A).
slides.title: Listening A

runs.t: How many? When is the rent due?

slides.notes:
Listen 2 (Task B): learners circle how many bedrooms and bathrooms. Listen 3 (Task C): when is the rent due?
Pairs compare. Then click to show each answer.
Task B: bedrooms 2, bathrooms 1 ("There are two bedrooms and one bathroom.").
Task C: on the first ("The rent is due on the first of the month.").
Say it with a partner (page D): "Is there a refrigerator?" "Yes, there is." / "No, there isn't." "How many bedrooms are there?" "There are two."
If behind: play the audio 2 times, and do Task C together.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson10/Level1_Lesson10.md (Step 3: Listening; Student Pages: Listening B, C, D; Answer key).
slides.title: Listening B + C

slides.notes:
Show the Grammar page. Box 1: "There is a kitchen. There is a bed." Click. "There are two bedrooms. There are chairs." Click.
Write on the board: one → is; two or more → are. Learners repeat.
Spanish hay = there is / there are (two English forms). Learners can read the Spanish note on their Grammar page.
Yes, use a for one countable thing: There is a bed.
Check questions: "There ___ a table." (is) • "There ___ two chairs." (are)
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson10/Level1_Lesson10.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Box 1; Grammar Box 1; Questions and answers; Teacher notes).

slides.title: There is / There are

slides.notes:
Left = question. Right = answer. Point left, then right.
Box 2: "Is there a sofa?" Click: "Yes, there is." / "No, there isn't." "Is there a washing machine?" Click: "No, there isn't."
Box 3: "Are there windows?" Click: "Yes, there are." / "No, there aren't." "How many bedrooms are there?" Click: "There are two."
One thing → Is there…? Two or more → Are there…?
Check question: "___ there a sofa?" (Is)
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson10/Level1_Lesson10.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Boxes 2–3; Grammar Boxes 2 and 3).

slides.title: Is there…? Are there…?

slides.notes:
Box 4: "Is there a bed?" Click: "Yes, there is." / "No, there isn't." "Are there chairs?" Click: "Yes, there are." / "No, there aren't."
Box 5 (side card): rooms + in the: "There is a table in the kitchen. There are two windows in the bedroom."
Pair drill (last 3–4 min): A looks at the floor plan; B asks Is there…? Are there…? How many…? Switch. If behind: skip the pair drill; Talk Time practices the same language.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson10/Level1_Lesson10.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, pair drill; Grammar Boxes 4 and 5).

runs.t: Do I say a with there is?

shapes.name: Floor plan: bedroom, kitchen, bathroom,  picture
shapes.alt: floor plan: bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, living room

slides.notes:
How is this different from Spanish? Spanish hay is one word. English has two forms: there is and there are. Click to show.
Right box: "Do I say a with there is?" Click: "Yes for one countable thing: There is a bed."
Point to the floor plan: "There is a kitchen. There is a bathroom. Is there a living room? Yes, there is."
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson10/Level1_Lesson10.md (Grammar: Questions and answers; Teacher notes).

slides.title: is or are?

runs.t: Write is, are, Is, or Are.

slides.notes:
Learners write is, are, Is, or Are on lines 1–5. Then pairs check.
Click to show each answer: 1 is, 2 are, 3 Is, 4 Are, 5 are (How many bedrooms are there?).
Lines 6–7 on the page: write one sentence with There is… and one with There are… (answers will vary).
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson10/Level1_Lesson10.md (Grammar: Practice; Answer key, Grammar practice; Grammar Box 3).
slides.title: is, are, Is, Are?

slides.notes:
Read each "Don't say" line. Shake your head. Click to show the correct line. Learners repeat it.
Have two bedrooms → There are two bedrooms. There is two beds → There are two beds. Is there windows? → Are there windows?
Big mistake this week: Have two bedrooms / There is two beds. Point to Grammar Box 1.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson10/Level1_Lesson10.md (Grammar: Common mistakes; Teacher notes).

runs.t: Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.

slides.notes:
Part 1, floor plan (6 min). A–B pairs. A looks at the floor plan (Student A page); partners don't show it. B asks and draws or writes. Then compare. Then switch.
B asks: Is there a kitchen? How many bedrooms are there? Is there a washing machine? Are there windows? A answers from the plan: Yes, there is. / No, there isn't. / There are ___.
Click to show each step.
Learners who can't write yet: they point on the floor plan and say "Yes, there is."
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson10/Level1_Lesson10.md (Step 5: Talk Time, Part 1; Student Pages: Talk Time A and B; Teacher notes).

slides.title: Talk Time

slides.notes:
Part 2, dream home (3 min). Each learner says 3 sentences about a dream home: There is… There are…
Model: "There is a kitchen." Click: "There are two bedrooms."
The partner can ask: Is there ___? How many ___ are there? Then switch.
A dream home is fine. Never ask for real rent or real addresses.
If behind: do half of Talk Time only.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson10/Level1_Lesson10.md (Step 5: Talk Time, Part 2; Student Pages: Talk Time B, Dream home; Teacher notes).
slides.title: Dream Home

slides.notes:
Exit ticket (never skip): each learner says "There is a ___." or "There are ___." Copying is fine.
Homework (10 minutes): open the Homework page. Do item 1, line 1 together. Point to each instruction.
Homework: 1) write about a home (yours or a dream home; never write a real rent amount if you don't want to); 2) write is or are; 3) draw a simple floor plan and label 3 rooms; 4) ask a family member "Is there a table in the kitchen?" and write the answer; 5) review: write today's date (Lesson 9).
Homework answers (answer key, Homework 2): 1 is, 2 are, 3 is, 4 are.

Learners answer. Then click to show each answer (answer key): 2 bedrooms, 1 bathroom, $900 per month.

slides.notes:
Read it (4 min), Task B: abbreviations. Learners match each one to a, b, or c.
Then click to show each answer: 2 BR → b bedrooms; 1 BA → a bathroom; /mo → c per month.
If behind: do Tasks A and B only.

slides.notes:
Task C: learners read the ad and circle Yes or No. Click to show each answer (answer key): 1 Yes, 2 Yes (the ad: 2 BR, 1 BA).
Task D (pairs): A asks "How many bedrooms?" B answers from the ad: "There are two." Then switch.

slides.title: Yes or No?

slides.notes:
Progress Check (5 min). Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read each word slowly, 2 times: 1 apartment, 2 kitchen, 3 sofa, 4 bedroom, 5 window. Learners circle.
Parts B and C: learners match and write on their own. Help with the instructions only. Click to show the Part B answers when you check together: 1 b, 2 c, 3 a, 4 d.
Part C answers: 1 is, 2 are, 3 Is, 4 Are.
Part D: read each "I can…" line and point to the 3 faces. Learners check one.
Score: A /5 + B /4 + C /4 = /13. Not a test grade. Collect if you want. If behind: do it next week at 6:00.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson10/Level1_Lesson10.md (Progress Check step; Student Pages: Progress Check; Answer key).
